description: Go library and server that put PostgreSQL behind POST /sql and a WebSocket tunnel, the request and response shapes the @neondatabase/serverless driver sends, plus a written protocol spec and a conformance corpus that checks any server over the network.
rules: Point neon() at the server with neonConfig.fetchEndpoint = "http://localhost:4000/sql", and Pool or Client at the tunnel with neonConfig.wsProxy = "localhost:4000/v2".
Set neonConfig.pipelineConnect = false when the database uses SCRAM. The driver's default connect pipelining assumes a cleartext password request and hangs otherwise.
Expect int8 and numeric values as JSON strings, not numbers: a JSON number is a double and loses precision beyond 2^53.
One admission function decides which database a request reaches: HTTPAdmission for NewHTTPHandler, Admission for the Echo NewHandler. Return an *AdmissionError to choose a refusal's HTTP status.
Give the WebSocket tunnel its own admission with WithHTTPWebSocketAdmission or WithWebSocketAdmission. StaticHTTPUpstream reads credentials from a request header the tunnel does not carry.
Upstream TLS is on by default. For a database that does not serve TLS, return an Upstream with TLSMode: pgserverless.TLSDisable from your own admission.
There is no connection pooling: each POST /sql request opens and closes its own database connection. Put a pooler in front of a database that cannot take that.
For a ready server in front of one database, run go install github.com/sferarc/pgserverless/cmd/pgserverless@latest and start it with DATABASE_URL set. It listens on 127.0.0.1:4000.
spec/SPEC.md is the only normative text and wins where openapi.yaml differs. Check any server against spec/cases/v1.json with go run ./cmd/pgsconform.
